subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey reject with 409, queue/serialize, or remain parallel by default, and should that behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The choice changes the public HTTP contract and retry behavior for existing webhook integrations and overlaps with broader persistent-session and queued-webhook designs.

options.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Introduce an explicit hook or mapping policy for same-sessionKey active deliveries while preserving current parallel acceptance by default.

options.title: Fold into queued webhooks
options.body: Treat this as part of the queued webhook design so backlog and concurrency controls own the retry/serialization contract.

options.title: Use unconditional 409
options.body: Make same-sessionKey active deliveries conflict everywhere, accepting a breaking change for current callers that rely on parallel 200/runId responses.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Introduce an explicit hook or mapping policy for same-sessionKey active deliveries while preserving current parallel acceptance by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is the public hook API/session policy shape, and steipete is the strongest product-boundary owner signal in the related review context.
